html:
Switzerland is a small federal state in the Alps, made of cantons with their own laws and four national languages: German, French, Italian and Romansh. On the map it appears from 1815, when the Congress of Vienna fixed its borders and recognised its permanent neutrality.

It grew out of the Old Swiss Confederacy, a league of valleys and towns that began in 1291 and broke away from the Holy Roman Empire in practice long before this was recognised in 1648. In 1798 the French replaced it with the Helvetic Republic, a central state that did not last.

After a short civil war between Catholic and Protestant cantons in 1847, the constitution of 1848 created the modern federal state with Bern as its capital. Swiss voters decide many laws directly by referendum.

Neutrality shaped its role in the world:

  • Henri Dunant founded the Red Cross in Geneva in 1863.
  • Geneva hosted the League of Nations after 1920.
  • It stayed out of both world wars, and its banks became a famous safe haven for money.

Swiss women got the vote in federal elections only in 1971. Switzerland joined the United Nations in 2002 and has stayed out of the European Union.
